paper.title_en: Is DESI Seeing Dynamical Dark Energy, or a Cosmic Glitch in Gravity?
paper.abstract_en: Combined baryon acoustic oscillation and cosmic microwave background data have begun to mildly favor departures from $Λ\mathrm{CDM}$. This is usually framed as 2-parameter dynamical dark energy. However, a 1-parameter "cosmic glitch in gravity" model, whose cosmological gravitational coupling differs from Newton's constant as in Hořava gravity, fits at least as well. $\textit{Planck}$+ACT+SPT and DESI~DR2 give $G_\mathrm{cosmo}/G_\mathrm{N}=0.9920\pm0.0025$, a $3.3\,σ$ preference for weaker cosmological gravity, robust to adding CMB lensing and supernovae. Fitted to the CMB alone, the glitch predicts DESI distances; $w_0w_a$CDM does not.
